text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is defined as a reading of 130/80 mm Hg or higher.
According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and major health organizations, blood pressure readings are grouped into distinct categories:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Elevated: Systolic between 120–129 and diastolic less than 80
Stage 1 Hypertension: Systolic 130–139 OR diastolic 80–89 mm Hg
Stage 2 Hypertension: Systolic 140 or higher OR diastolic 90 or higher mm Hg
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 systolic and/or higher than 120 diastolic (requires immediate medical care)

text_blocks.snippet: Note: The top number is systolic (pressure when the heart beats) and the bottom number is diastolic (pressure when the heart rests between beats).
